Author: M.M. Sundresh
Bench: M.M. Sundresh

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction

 (arising out of Slp (Crl.) No.2293 of 2020)
 Aakash Aggarwal ..... Appella
 Versus
 Anjali Aggarwal & Anr. ..... Respond
O R D E R
Leave granted.
Parties have entered into a compromise vide Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023 under the aegis of the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.
The appellant  Aakash Aggarwal and respondent no.1  Anjali Aggarwal are present in the Court today and have been identified by the learned counsel for the parties.
The parties in person admit their signature and accept the terms and conditions mentioned in the Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023.

Learned counsel for the parties jointly state that the Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023 may be taken on record and appropriate orders may be passed by this Court in exercise of the power of this Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
The appellant  Aakash Aggarwal and respondent no.1  Anjali Aggarwal had got married on 23.01.2003 and they have been residing and living separately since 2017.
In view of the Settlement Agreement, we pass the decree of divorce by mutual consent dissolving the marriage between the appellant  Aakash Aggarwal and respondent no.1 - Anjali Aggarwal in exercise of the power of this Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.

Aakash Aggarwal vs Anjali Aggarwal on 17 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132097636/
1

Appellant  Aakash Aggarwal has already made a payment of Rs.30,00,000/- (Rupees thirty lakhs only), by way of demand draft(s), in terms of sub-clauses (a) and (b) of paragraph/clause 2 of the Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023.
Respondent no.1  Anjali Aggarwal accepts that she has received these payments.

Appellant  Aakash Aggarwal has handed-over to the Respondent No.1- Anjali Aggarwal demand draft of Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees twenty lakhs only), drawn in favour of Registrar, Supreme Court of India, in terms of sub-clause (c) of paragraph/clause 2 of the Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023.
On encashment of this demand draft, the amount of Rs.20,00,000/- (Rupees twenty lakhs only) will be paid to respondent no.1  Anjali Aggarwal by the Registrar/Registry of this Court.

The appellant  Aakash Aggarwal has also handed-over to the Respondent No.1- Anjali Aggarwal demand draft of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakhs only) in favour of respondent no.2 - Shubh Aggarwal (minor child of the appellant  Aakash Aggarwal and the Respondent No.1- Anjali Aggarwal), in terms of sub-clause (d)(i) of paragraph/clause 2 of the Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023.
We are satisfied that the Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023 and the terms thereof are in the interest and for the benefit of respondent no.2 - Shubh Aggarwal/minor child.
Accordingly, we accord leave of this Court under Order XXXII Rule 7 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908.

Respondent no.1 - Anjali Aggarwal will file an affidavit before this Court, along with a certificate of the learned counsel/Advocate on Record appearing for respondent no.2 - Shubh Aggarwal/minor child, stating that the compromise/Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023, in her opinion, is for the benefit of respondent no.2 - Shubh Aggarwal/minor child.
The affidavit and certificate will be filed by respondent no.1 - Anjali Aggarwal and the Counsel/Advocate on Record within a period of ten days from today.

The parties will comply with the paragraphs/clauses 3, 4 and 5 and will be bound and abide by the Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023, which specifically records that the payments made to respondent no.1  Anjali Aggarwal are in full and final settlement of all her claims relating to the alimony, maintenance etc., including rights in the property i.e. Plot No. H-763-A, First Floor, Palam Vihar, Gurugram, Haryana.
The parties will also abide by the visitation rights given to the appellant  Aakash Aggarwal in terms of the compromise/Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023.
In terms of the compromise/Settlement Agreement dated 24.04.2023, the Partition suit No. CS 63 of 2019 filed by respondent no.1 - Anjali Aggarwal against the appellant  Aakash Aggarwal for partition and possession of the property situated at Plot No. H-763-A, First Floor, Palam Vihar,
Gurugram, Haryana, shall be treated as dismissed as withdrawn.

We also, hereby, deem it appropriate to pass an order quashing/dismissing as withdrawn the following proceedings initiated by the appellant  Aakash Aggarwal and respondent no.1 - Anjali Aggarwal:
